title: instrument-span-fanout-and-invocation-cost-explorer
author: Maya Thompson
description:
Context: Long-tail cost regressions and noisy token-level signals make it hard to triage why an invocation became expensive. We instrument a lightweight 'span fanout' sampler that, when an invocation exceeds a configurable cost threshold, opportunistically increases tracing sampling for its child spans and records token-level cost deltas and cache-effect annotations. Motivation: give SREs and on-call engineers an end-to-end view of per-invocation token cost and where the cost amplifies across the serving pipeline without permanently increasing global sampling rates. What this PR does: 1) runtime: add telemetry/span_fanout.go implementing a bounded fanout sampler that tags sampled spans with token_cost_delta, kv_cache_hits, model_variant and invocation_stage. The sampler respects per-tenant and per-route budgets and decays after the critical window. 2) metrics: introduce a token_cost_delta Prometheus metric and a compact histogram for per-invocation token timelines. 3) console: add a new dashboard JSON (Invocation Cost Explorer) that surfaces invocation timeline, span fanout tree, cumulative cost waterfall, and a sortable table of top contributing spans. 4) alerts: introduce tuned alert invocation-cost-regression which uses route-weighted thresholds and an exponential backoff to avoid noisy pages for known bursty routes. 5) docs + tests: add a docs page that explains the sampler knobs and a test harness to simulate fanout under quota constraints. Backwards compatibility: fanout is off by default and sampling respects existing global sampling settings. Rollout plan: staged enablement by tenant via feature flag and a 2-week canary with enhanced retention for fanout traces. Checklist:
- [x] implement fanout sampler and tagging
- [x] export token_cost_delta and histogram metrics
- [x] add dashboard JSON and panels
- [x] add alert with suppressions for bursty routes
- [x] unit + integration tests
- [x] docs and runbook entry

Notes on design decisions: the fanout sampler is intentionally conservative: it only amplifies sampling for direct child spans of a high-cost root invocation, has a strict max-per-invocation cap, and records an opaque fanout_id for cross-join in downstream systems. Token-level cost deltas are stored as delta-per-stage to make comparisons across model variants easier. The dashboard is intentionally focused on forensics (single-invocation deep-dive) rather than rollup aggregates; rollups will be a follow-up. Related work: builds on prior token-span-attribution work (see ENG-1310) and complements the Invocation Fingerprint panels. Migration & ops: new config keys added to telemetry config; default shown in docs; ops should monitor the fanout_sampler.total_samples metric during rollout.

alerts: add invocation-cost-regression alert with route-weighting
tests: add span_fanout test harness and synthetic invocation generator
docs: add observability/invocation-explorer.md and runbook notes

chore: lint and dashboard schema validation fixes
review_comments: Arjun: Nice work — can you explain how fanout interacts with tenant-level sampling budgets? I don't want this to blow a tenant's budget during a traffic spike.
Maya: The fanout sampler checks a per-tenant token budget and refuses to amplify if remaining budget < configured_minimum. I added tests for budget exhaustion paths.
Sofia: Dashboard looks useful but the initial panel layout is dense. Can we collapse the span tree by default and add a 'show full tree' toggle?
Maya: Updated the dashboard JSON to collapse deeper levels and added the toggle as requested (see commit 6).
Liam: CI flaky test in span_fanout_test.go failed on first run (timing). We should use a deterministic clock in tests.
Maya: Switched to a deterministic clock in tests and reran CI. All green now.
SRE: small ops question — what metrics should we watch during canary?
Maya: Monitor fanout_sampler.total_samples, fanout_sampler.rejected_by_budget, token_cost_delta:sum and kv_cache_hits:rate — added to runbook.
release_notes: Introduces a conservative span fanout sampler that increases tracing for high-cost invocations, exports token_cost_delta metrics, and adds the Invocation Cost Explorer dashboard. Disabled by default; opt-in via feature flag. Ops: monitor fanout_sampler.* metrics during rollout.
